findings.reason: a builder can land the two scrubs the done-when does test and close the section with the fleet route still leaking the session identity, which is the exact defect the section exists to close.
findings.text: §49's deliverable lists four mechanisms, and its done-when (a) tests only the `subprocess.Popen` route of `_start_watch_producer` (which passes no `env=`); the fourth, "the supervisor script `_WATCH_PRODUCER_SUPERVISOR` removes them before it starts the producer, so the fleet route is covered too", is never exercised because the supervisor is launched by the allocation's batch step, not by `_start_watch_producer`, and `_spawn_through_fleet` carries no environment — so the property that covers the fleet route (the route this very node runs under) can stay unimplemented while every case passes

findings.reason: the done-when cases pin the observable behaviour, so a builder taking the literal reading is corrected by (c) before the section can close.
findings.text: §50's deliverable says a stale re-arm "resumes as a baseline at the stream's end", but `_follow_resume_plan`'s baseline mode derives the fleet report from live run state and never seeks to the stream's end, and a literal seek to the end would draw none of the rows of a run that changed during the stale margin, which done-when (c) requires
